$comment: Ten archetypes. Each is a coherent, human-verified stack: not a weighted fruit salad. proto = target position on each axis (0..1). weight = how much that axis matters for this archetype. Blueprint copy is warm-tease by design.

archetypes.name: xXArchWizardXx
archetypes.tagline: You don't install Arch. You slowly become it.
archetypes.annoy: You will say "btw" unprompted. There is no known cure.
archetypes.hardwareNone: A used ThinkPad, pre-scratched. Buying pristine hardware for this archetype is like buying ironed jeans.
archetypes.alt: Gentoo, if even Arch feels too pre-chewed.

archetypes.name: The Rice Farmer
archetypes.tagline: You will spend four hours making the terminal transparent. Worth it.

blueprint.v: Bottles, for that one app you won't admit to
you will handle that part yourself

archetypes.annoy: Your own perfectionism. The rice is never done. You know this.
archetypes.hardwareNone: Framework Laptop 13: repairable, and the screenshots will match the hardware's taste level.
archetypes.alt: EndeavourOS, if you want closer-to-vanilla Arch under the rice.

archetypes.name: The Escapee
archetypes.tagline: You didn't leave Apple. Apple left you, one Tahoe at a time.

blueprint.v: Omarchy: Arch with taste, batteries included
Hyprland, pre-themed. Someone with taste already suffered for you
your web apps never left the browser anyway
keyboard shortcuts that finally make sense

archetypes.annoy: Two weeks of muscle-memory fights. Cmd is Super now. Breathe.
archetypes.hardwareNone: Framework Laptop 13 Pro: CNC aluminum, 20-hour battery, ships with Linux. The MacBook build quality argument is over.
archetypes.alt: Fedora Workstation, if you would rather have a big-tent default than one person's opinionated setup.

archetypes.name: The Civilian
archetypes.tagline: The computer is an appliance. This one just refuses to show you ads.

blueprint.v: Cinnamon: looks like the computer you already know
Steam + Proton, if it comes to that
LibreOffice + the browser you already live in
you will never need to open it (it's there, though)
updates that ask politely and mean it

archetypes.annoy: Friends who use Arch will call this boring. They rebuild their audio stack on weekends. You have a life.
archetypes.hardwareNone: A refurbished ThinkPad or a Slimbook: quiet, certified, done.
archetypes.alt: Fedora Workstation, if your laptop is very new and you want the modern stack at the cost of a slightly less familiar desktop.

archetypes.name: The Grandpa
archetypes.tagline: It will outlive both of us, and it knows it.

blueprint.v: Xfce: unchanged since your favorite decade
you escaped in 2009 and never looked back

archetypes.annoy: Your software is two years old. So is your peace of mind. Fair trade.
archetypes.hardwareNone: Any ThinkPad from the last decade. It will match your energy: unglamorous, indestructible.
archetypes.alt: Ubuntu LTS, if you want the biggest support ecosystem and can make peace with snaps.

archetypes.name: The Gamer
archetypes.tagline: Windows was just a launcher with ads. You're replacing a launcher.

blueprint.v: Steam + Proton + Gamescope. This is why you are here
a small Windows partition for the anticheat holdouts: an airlock, not a home
once a year, to paste one Proton flag
the controller works before you finish sitting down

archetypes.annoy: That one kernel-anticheat title. Blame its publisher, not the penguin.
archetypes.hardwareNone: A Steam Deck if you travel, a Beelink or Minisforum box with AMD graphics if you don't.
archetypes.alt: CachyOS, if you want to turn the performance knobs yourself.

archetypes.name: The Pro
archetypes.tagline: You bill by the hour. The OS should be invisible.

blueprint.v: Steam exists here too, after hours
containers ate your Windows needs years ago

archetypes.annoy: GNOME will remove a feature you liked. There is an extension. There is always an extension.
archetypes.hardwareNone: Framework Laptop 13 Pro or a Linux-certified ThinkPad. Warranty, docks, no surprises.
archetypes.alt: Ubuntu LTS, if your employer's tooling assumes it.

archetypes.name: The Suckless Monk
archetypes.tagline: You count RAM megabytes the way others count calories.

blueprint.v: sway: one config file, zero decoration
roguelikes, in the terminal, as intended
a status bar with exactly the four numbers you need

archetypes.annoy: You will spend a weekend removing things that were not hurting you.
archetypes.hardwareNone: A used ThinkPad X-series. Small, matte, silent. Like you.
archetypes.alt: Alpine, if even glibc feels indulgent.

archetypes.name: The Declarative
archetypes.tagline: You will rebuild your entire machine from one file, and you will tell everyone.

blueprint.v: your choice: declared in one file
configuration.nix: your entire computer as a text file

archetypes.annoy: The documentation. Everyone says it. Everyone is right.
archetypes.hardwareNone: Anything. The config outlives the hardware.
archetypes.alt: Guix, if you would rather declare your universe in Scheme.

archetypes.name: The Necromancer
archetypes.tagline: That 2014 laptop was never dead. It was waiting.

blueprint.v: Linux Mint Xfce: or antiX for the truly departed
emulators of consoles this machine once envied
this machine owes Windows nothing anymore
htop, open purely to admire the free RAM
a battery that suddenly lasts hours again

archetypes.annoy: You will start rescuing other people's old laptops. Your shelf is not ready.
archetypes.hardwareNone: You specifically do not buy hardware. Someone's closet already holds your next machine.
archetypes.alt: Debian + LXQt, if you want to go even lighter than Xfce.
